counter_trend_prerequisites.llm_summary: Before trading counter-trend, 4 elements must be understood: (1) Valid Inducement of Major Trend — where smart money traps retail, essential for all counter-trend decisions. (2) Fair Value Gap (FVG) — FVG tells market intention, where smart money wants to move. (3) Opposing HTF Point of Interest (POI) — if H4 is bullish, know where daily/weekly sell zones are above current price. (4) Where is Market Price Actually? Three states: (a) Rejecting from trending POI zone, (b) Retracing back to trending POI zone, (c) Has done Break of Structure or not. Counter-trend gains are smaller than trend trades — risk is similar but reward is comparatively less. However, with good command, you can achieve low risk and high reward even in counter-trend. The presenter recommends: pick your TF combination, stick with it for an extended period, backtest it.
key_rules: 4 prerequisites: Valid IDM, FVG understanding, Opposing HTF POI, Market price location
Know where major trend's inducement is — SM traps retail there
FVG tells market intention (direction SM wants to move)
Know opposing HTF POI zones against your trading TF trend
Market price has 3 states: rejecting from POI, retracing to POI, BOS done or not
Counter-trend = smaller gains vs trending, but still good R:R with command
TF combinations: Positional (Monthly/Daily), Swing (Weekly/H4), Short Term (Daily/H1), Intra-day (H4/M30), Day Trading (H1/M15), Scalping (M15/M5)
Pick one combination and stick for extended period

counter_trend_rules_bearish.llm_summary: When market is bearish and sell zones are far from inducement, counter-trend buy trades can capture the pullback. 3 Rules: (1) Major trend (H4) must close candle body ABOVE its first valid inducement. When H4 closes above its own IDM → market will retrace upward (counter-trend). (2) A Fair Value Gap must exist in the swing where market closed above IDM. The FVG in that swing confirms market intention and makes the counter-trend high probability. (3) On LTF (M15), after IDM candle body close → map counter-trend IDM → when market taps FVG and closes above → counter-trend established → look for entry confirmations (MSS, SCOB, swing-based CHoCH). Range definition: from the high where market rejected to the low where market's candle body closed above IDM → this becomes the swing range. Draw Premium/Discount zones (50% level). Counter-trend target = FIRST sell zone above IDM or the 50% level of the swing. NEVER hold counter-trend beyond the first sell zone — take profit and release the trade. If market does BOS on LTF → deeper pullback indicated → can continue counter-trend entries. The bullish market counter-trend (selling into H4 buy zone) is the exact mirror.
key_rules: Rule 1: Major trend candle body close ABOVE its first valid IDM → counter-trend starts
Rule 2: FVG must exist in the swing that closed above IDM → high probability
Rule 3: LTF entry confirmation needed (MSS, SCOB, or swing-based CHoCH)
Range: rejected high ↔ IDM close low = swing range → draw Premium/Discount (50%)
Counter-trend target = FIRST sell zone above IDM or 50% equilibrium level
NEVER hold counter-trend beyond first opposing zone — take profit and exit
LTF BOS confirmed → deeper pullback → can continue counter-trend entries
Bullish counter-trend (bearish pullback) = exact mirror of bearish
Counter-trend entry after IDM close + FVG + LTF confirmation = high probability

real_chart_counter_trend_gbpusd.llm_summary: Complete GBP/USD demonstration using H4 (major bullish trend) and M15 (counter-trend sell). Setup: H4 bullish with BOS confirmed. IDM marked. Buy zones far below (Order Block + FVG, and extreme Order Block). Market has moved far from buy zones → counter-trend sell opportunity. HTF confirmation: Daily chart shows Order Block rejection at the high → market rejecting from Daily OB = strong evidence for counter-trend. H4: IDM close below confirmed → 3 rules satisfied (IDM close + FVG in swing + Daily OB rejection). M15 counter-trend execution: (1) Mark M15 counter-trend IDM. (2) Wait for structure shift after IDM close. (3) OB near IDM has no immediate liquidity → expect sweep. (4) Market sweeps OB → previous high liquidity swept → SCOB forms. First SCOB entry: at retest, SL above SCOB high (2-3 pips), TP at the low from which market rose to sweep. Aggressive drop → TP hit. Second SCOB entry: market retraces → new SCOB at retest → TP hit again. After counter-trend BOS: deeper pullback confirmed → mark new M15 IDM → M15 Lower High marked as change of character invalidation level.
key_rules: GBP/USD H4 bullish + Daily OB rejection → counter-trend sell on M15
H4 IDM close below + FVG in swing + Daily rejection = 3 rules satisfied
M15: mark counter-trend IDM → wait for structure shift
OB with no immediate liquidity nearby → market will sweep it first
SCOB entry after previous high liquidity sweep → aggressive drop → TP hit
Second SCOB entry from retracement → TP hit → both counter-trend take profits achieved
Counter-trend BOS on LTF → deeper pullback → continue counter-trend entries
M15 Lower High = CHoCH invalidation level — if broken, back to trend direction

qml_in_counter_trend.llm_summary: When no unmitigated Order Block exists above the IDM in counter-trend, use QML Level as the POI zone. In the GBP/USD example: after counter-trend BOS, new IDM marked on M15. Above the IDM, no unmitigated OB available → use QML Level (Quasimodo Level) as the sell zone. The QML Level sits below the M15 Lower High (LH). At QML Level: (a) wait for IDM sweep → SCOB entry, or (b) take direct entry at QML Level because risk is defined (SL above LH — if LH breaks, market resumes trend). QML provides excellent risk-to-reward because SL is tight (above LH) and TP is at the swing low. This connects to V18 (POI Zones) where QML was introduced as the 3rd priority POI zone used when no FVG or OB is available.
key_rules: When no unmitigated OB above IDM → use QML Level as POI zone
QML Level sits below M15 Lower High (LH)
At QML: either wait for IDM sweep + SCOB, or take direct entry
Direct entry OK because risk defined: SL above LH (if broken = trend resumes)
QML provides excellent R:R — tight SL, wide TP to swing low
QML is 3rd priority POI zone (from V18): used when no FVG or OB available

multiple_scob_counter_trend_entries.llm_summary: The real chart demonstration shows a systematic approach of taking multiple counter-trend SCOB entries along the M15 structure: (1) First SCOB: after IDM sweep → previous high liquidity swept → SCOB forms → sell at retest → TP at previous low → hit. (2) Second SCOB: market retraces → new SCOB at IDM retest → sell → TP hit. (3) Counter-trend BOS confirmed → deeper pullback → new IDM marked. (4) Third SCOB: at IDM sweep → SCOB forms near QML level → sell → TP hit. (5) Fourth SCOB: after new BOS → new IDM → SCOB forms → sell at retest → 1:3.6 R:R. (6) Fifth entry: at Order Block near new IDM → 1:7.2 R:R achieved. Counter-trend stops when market reaches H4 buy zone (Order Block). Key recommendation: one pair = one trade at a time. The presenter emphasizes: do NOT overtrade — take one SCOB entry, achieve TP, then reassess. Multiple entries shown for education only. Safe SL = above SCOB high (2-3 pips) or above the most recent LTF LH for wider but safer placement.
key_rules: Systematic SCOB entries along M15 counter-trend structure
Each entry: IDM sweep → SCOB forms → sell at retest → TP at previous low
After BOS on LTF: mark new IDM → continue counter-trend entries
Counter-trend stops at H4 buy zone (Order Block) — do NOT sell below it
Risk-reward achievable: 1:2.5 to 1:7.2 on individual counter-trend entries
Recommendation: one pair = one trade at a time — avoid overtrading
Safe SL: above SCOB high (2-3 pips) or above most recent LTF Lower High
When LH is broken → CHoCH back to trend direction → stop counter-trend
OB with no immediate liquidity nearby = market will sweep it first — wait
Previous high/low liquidity sweep makes SCOB very effective
